statement: Clinical guidance shifted away from alcohol/antiseptic cord care toward dry cord care; alcohol does not reduce omphalitis risk and is associated with a longer cord separation time, so a parent following an older generation's 'wipe it with alcohol' habit is following superseded advice.
evidence: Meta-analysis (Al-Shehri, Cureus 2019, PMID 31523534): alcohol 70% vs dry care, 13 studies / 4967 infants / 6 RCTs — alcohol significantly associated with longer cord separation time (MD +1.93 days, 95% CI 0.80-3.06) with no significant difference in omphalitis risk. WHO Essential Newborn Care (2024) and Merck Manual present dry care as standard.
source: PMID 31523534 (Cureus 2019); WHO ENC provider guide May 2024; Merck Manual
